q: We argue the unit of comparison for human-centered coding-agent evaluation should be the harness–model pair, not the model alone
r: Include: controlled comparison of harnesses with model fixed, with token-cost metrics and repeated trials, so the contribution is the evaluation method.

q: agents implement a REST API server and modify it across a tunable number of procedurally generated follow-up change requests
r: Include: new benchmark where agents build and extend an application over 100 change requests, with paired statistics across six harnesses and seven models.

q: ICAE-Bench, an benchmark for evaluating coding agents under interactive project-building settings
r: Include: project-level repository generation from fuzzy natural-language requirements across 12 languages; new interactive evaluation design.

q: We introduce LOOPSBENCH, a long horizon benchmark for loop engineering in coding agent evaluation.
r: Include: new long-horizon benchmark with a new evaluation runtime and loop-trace metrics, comparing agent and loop configurations on multi-unit development tasks.

q: agents modify code repositories to complete requirements, and their patches are evaluated with tests
r: EC6: SWE-bench-style issue resolution (resolve rate, fail-to-pass tests) with added clarification and planning references, so issue repair.

q: Evaluation and operation are therefore treated as a dependency chain in which weaknesses in task construction, execution environments, retrieval, state management, verification, or observability can invalidate conclusions made downstream.
r: Include: secondary multivocal review on evaluating and operating coding agents (variance, baselines, cost, memory), relevant to RQ2-RQ4.

q: GameGen evaluates game creation from natural-language requirements
r: EC6: benchmark limited to one specialised domain (game development), with a bug-repair track and no contribution to the evaluation method beyond the domain benchmark.

q: A three-stage evaluation protocol measures both migration completeness and behavioural correctness.
r: Include: whole-repository code migration (not issue repair), and the main contribution is a new three-stage evaluation protocol with agentic verification over 520 runs.

q: DeltaSelect is intended for repeated baseline-versus-candidate comparisons during development, not model rankings.
r: Include: the contribution is an evaluation method (cost-aware task selection, run-to-run variance, calibrated scores) for comparing coding-agent configurations.

q: We introduce GameLogicBench, a benchmark of 72 gameplay-logic tasks in Godot projects.
r: EC6: benchmark limited to one specialised domain (Godot game logic), mainly a domain benchmark rather than a general evaluation-method contribution.
